sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代夜总会打碟的日子里，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成一个美丽的、有50年历史的手工艺品的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: All week, Senate Democrats have furiously protested the decision by Republicans to protect thousands of documents related to Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 整个星期，参议院民主党人对共和党人为保护数千份与最高法院大法官提名人布雷特·卡瓦诺相关的文件而做出的决定进行了愤怒的抗议。

sentences.en: On the third day of his hearing, that fury came to a head.
sentences.zh: 在他听证会的第三天，这种愤怒达到了顶峰。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月7日，星期五。

sentences.en: Adam Liptak.
sentences.zh: 亚当·利普塔克。

sentences.en: Documents have dominated this week of Senate confirmation hearings for Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 文件一直是本周布雷特·卡瓦诺参议院听证会的主导话题。

sentences.en: Documents that haven't been made available.
sentences.zh: 那些尚未公开的文件。

sentences.en: Documents that have been made available, but at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 那些已经公开但却是在最后一刻才公开的文件。

sentences.en: Documents that the senators have looked at but aren't actually allowed to talk about.
sentences.zh: 参议员们看过但实际上不允许谈论的文件。

sentences.en: How is it that documents became so central to this confirmation hearing?
sentences.zh: 文件怎么会成为这次确认听证会的核心呢？

sentences.en: Well, happening tomorrow, President Trump will be announcing his next nominee for the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 嗯，明天将要发生的是，特朗普总统将宣布他的下一位最高法院大法官提名人。

sentences.en: Even as President Trump was choosing among the four finalists for the job.
sentences.zh: 甚至在特朗普总统从四个最终人选挑选时也是如此。

sentences.en: On the president's shortlist of potential Supreme Court nominees, Judge Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 在总统的最高法院大法官潜在提名人短名单上，有法官布雷特·卡瓦诺。

sentences.en: Critics of Kavanaugh suggest he's been part of the establishment for too long.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺的批评者认为他成为建制派的时间太长了。

sentences.en: People were warning him that a negative, a downside of choosing Judge Brett Kavanaugh, was that there were literally millions of documents.
sentences.zh: 人们警告他，选择布雷特·卡瓦诺法官的一个负面因素、一个缺点是，那里有字面意义上数百万份文件。

sentences.en: Brett Kavanaugh's confirmation, it could get slowed down if senators want to review his lengthy record as a judge,
sentences.zh: 布雷特·卡瓦诺的确认，如果参议员们想要审查他作为法官的冗长记录，可能会放慢速度，

sentences.en: as well as all the presidential documents that would have crossed his desk when he worked for President George W.
sentences.zh: 以及所有在他为乔治·W·总统工作时经过他办公桌的总统文件。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 布什。

sentences.en: Judge Kavanaugh served in the Bush White House for five years, two years in the White House Counsel's Office, about three years as staff secretary.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺法官在布什白宫服务了五年，两年在白宫法律顾问办公室，大约三年担任办公厅秘书。

sentences.en: The Senate must now be able to have access to adequately review all documents, emails, other paperwork associated with Judge Kavanaugh before the process moves forward.
sentences.zh: 在程序推进之前，参议院现在必须能够获得并充分审查与卡瓦诺法官相关的所有文件、电子邮件和其他纸质文件。

sentences.en: We're talking about lots and lots of documents.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是成堆成堆的文件。

sentences.en: He's one of 15 people on an email chain and every person on that email chain produces the documents and there's a lot of duplication and nonsense.
sentences.zh: 他是某个电邮链中的15个人之一，这个电邮链中的每个人都会产生文件，其中有大量的重复和废话。

sentences.en: That the paper trail, just the sheer volume of it could be used against him, not even what's in it.
sentences.zh: 这些纸质记录，仅仅是其庞大的数量就可以用来反对他，甚至不管里面写了什么。

sentences.en: Literally millions of documents.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的数百万份文件。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And why are the documents seen as a problem, given that this is a Republican-controlled Senate that's expected to confirm Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 鉴说这是一个预计会确认卡瓦诺的共和党控制的参议院，为什么这些文件被视为一个问题？

sentences.en: Well, they want to move quickly, and there may be three reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们想要迅速行动，这可能有三个原因。

sentences.en: One is that they may want to get him on the court when the court comes back on the first Monday in October.
sentences.zh: 一个是他们可能希望当法院在10月第一个星期一回归时，让他进入法院。

sentences.en: But the early sittings of the court don't have any interesting cases on them.
sentences.zh: 但法院早期的开庭并没有什么有趣的案件。

sentences.en: So I don't know that that really matters.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道这是否真的重要。

sentences.en: A second possibility is they fear, however remote the chance is, that the Senate will flip after the midterms and they want to make sure they get their guy on.
sentences.zh: 第二个可能性是他们担心，无论机会多么渺茫，参议院可能会在期中选举后翻盘，他们想确保把他们的人安插进去。

sentences.en: And there are people who say they want to make sure that Kavanaugh is on the court should a dispute between Bob Mueller, the special counsel,
sentences.zh: 并且有人说，他们希望确保如果特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒之间的争端，

sentences.en: and President Trump reach the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 与特朗普总统的争端到达最高法院时，卡瓦诺已经在法院里。

sentences.en: So that speed comes into conflict with the volume of documents that follow behind Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种速度与卡瓦诺身后的巨量文件发生了冲突。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just to be sure I understand, why exactly?
sentences.zh: 为了确保我理解清楚，究竟是为什么？

sentences.en: What is it about this many documents that seems that difficult for everyone involved in the process?
sentences.zh: 这么多文件到底有什么问题，让参与这个过程的每个人都觉得如此困难？

sentences.en: Because in my mind, a truck backs up to the National Archives, the documents go in, and it drives across the street to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，一辆卡车倒车开到国家档案馆，文件装进去，然后开过街到参议院。

sentences.en: So the National Archives has to process these documents and make sure that they shouldn't be withheld for many legitimate reasons, executive privilege,
sentences.zh: 所以国家档案馆必须处理这些文件，并确保出于许多正当理由不应隐瞒这些文件，比如行政特权、

sentences.en: various kinds of confidentiality, personal information.
sentences.zh: 各种保密性、个人信息。

sentences.en: And nobody disputes that they need to go through a process.
sentences.zh: 没有人否认他们需要经历一个流程。

sentences.en: And the National Archives, even though they've only been asked for a portion of these documents, said it can't get it done in time.
sentences.zh: 而国家档案馆，尽管只被要求提供这些文件的一部分，却表示无法及时完成。

sentences.en: President George W.
sentences.zh: 乔治·W·总统

sentences.en: Bush's personal lawyer has taken up this task and, with the help of many others, has produced a lot of documents.
sentences.zh: 布什的私人律师承担了这项任务，在许多其他人的帮助下，产生了大量文件。

sentences.en: But Democrats complain that that's a weird process,
sentences.zh: 但民主党人抱怨说这是一个奇怪的流程，

sentences.en: that you have someone who seems like a partisan in charge of getting stuff done quickly rather than waiting for the National Archives, which is to say the federal government,
sentences.zh: 你有一个看起来像是党派人士的人负责快速完成工作，而不是等待国家档案馆，也就是联邦政府，

sentences.en: to do the job itself.
sentences.zh: 自己来做这项工作。

sentences.en: And so it's this partisan lawyer who's now involved in this process, who has been deciding what the Senate gets or doesn't get, and at what moment in this process they get it.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是这个党派律师参与了这个过程，他一直在决定参议院得到什么或得不到什么，以及他们在过程的哪个时刻得到它。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Give us a sense, Adam, of how Democrats are talking about these documents before the hearings begin.
sentences.zh: 亚当，跟我们讲讲在听证会开始之前，民主党人是如何谈论这些文件的。

sentences.en: I am considering all the tools that are available to delay this nomination.
sentences.zh: 我正在考虑所有可用的工具来拖延这项提名。

sentences.en: So the first kinds of complaints are global complaints.
sentences.zh: 所以第一类抱怨是全局性的抱怨。

sentences.en: There's a wide range of relevant issues that we don't yet have a full insight into.
sentences.zh: 有一系列广泛的相关问题，我们尚未获得全面的了解。

sentences.en: So I don't think we should be going ahead on September 4th with the confirmation hearings.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们不应该在9月4日继续进行确认听证会。

sentences.en: We're not getting enough documents.
sentences.zh: 我们没有得到足够的文件。

sentences.en: We're not getting documents fast enough.
sentences.zh: 我们获取文件的速度不够快。

sentences.en: We're entitled to more documents.
sentences.zh: 我们有权获得更多的文件。

sentences.en: I believe Chairman Grassley has scheduled a hearing for Judge Kavanaugh too soon, and I am calling on him to delay the hearing.
sentences.zh: 我相信格拉斯利主席为卡瓦诺法官安排听证会的时间太早了，我呼吁他推迟听证会。

sentences.en: But as the hearings approach, there's a second kind of problem, which is some of the documents have been produced, but only to the committee and its staff,
sentences.zh: 但随着听证会的临近，出现了第二类问题，那就是有些文件已经产生，但只提供给委员会及其工作人员，

sentences.en: so-called committee confidential documents.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的委员会机密文件。

sentences.en: 148,000 documents that I've seen that you cannot see because they won't allow us to make them public.
sentences.zh: 我见过的148000份文件，你看不到，因为他们不允许我们将其公之于众。

sentences.en: And some of those documents are alive quite late, including on the Monday before the hearings, which is the Labor Day holiday.
sentences.zh: 其中一些文件直到很晚才生效，包括听证会前的星期一，也就是劳动节假期。

sentences.en: Do you think any of these documents could make him unqualified for the job?
sentences.zh: 你认为这些文件中的任何一份会让他不适合担任这个职务吗？

sentences.en: I think that you could ask some very interesting questions about these documents that I'm unable to even say because I'm not able to make them public.
sentences.zh: 我认为你可以对这些文件提出一些非常有趣的问题，但我甚至无法说出口，因为我无法将它们公之于众。

sentences.en: And some of those documents, Democrats say, look pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 民主党人说，其中一些文件看起来非常有趣。

sentences.en: They'd like to talk about them, but the rules suggest that they can't.
sentences.zh: 他们很想谈论它们，但规则表明他们不能。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So committee confidential means members of the Judiciary Committee can lay eyes on the documents, but they cannot talk about them in a way that would reveal their contents.
sentences.zh: 所以委员会机密意味着司法委员会成员可以过目这些文件，但他们不能以透露其内容的方式谈论它们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or at a minimum, they can't disclose the underlying documents so that then you run into these semantic questions of can you question the witness about an email from 15 years ago,
sentences.zh: 或者至少，他们不能披露基础文件，这样你就会遇到这些语义学问题：你能否就15年前的一封电子邮件质问证人，

sentences.en: but not show the witness the email?
sentences.zh: 但又不能把电子邮件给证人看？

sentences.en: It gets pretty confusing and almost Kafka-esque pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 这变得相当混乱，而且很快就几乎变得像卡夫卡小说一样荒诞。

sentences.en: So how does this actually start to play out on day one of these hearings?
sentences.zh: 那么这在这些听证会的第一天是如何开始展开的呢？

sentences.en: And you're rightly proud, Mr. Chairman, if we cannot be recognized, I move to adjourn.
sentences.zh: 主席先生，如果我们得不到承认，您是理所当然地引以为傲的，我动议休会。

sentences.en: On day one, when we just have opening statements, you have complaints about some of these issues.
sentences.zh: 在第一天，当我们只有开场陈述时，你就会听到对其中一些问题的抱怨。

sentences.en: We have been denied real access to the documents we need to advise...
sentences.zh: 我们被剥夺了获得我们所需文件的真正渠道，以提供咨询……

sentences.en: Mr. Chairman, regular orders call for...
sentences.zh: 主席先生，常规程序要求……

sentences.en: ...which turns this hearing into a charade and a mockery of our norMs.
sentences.zh: ……这把这场听证会变成了一场滑稽戏，对我们规范的嘲弄。

sentences.en: On day one of the questioning, which is to say day two of the hearings, Democratic senators start pushing their toe across the line and start referring to these documents.
sentences.zh: 在质询的第一天，也就是听证会的第二天，民主党参议员开始将脚趾踩过界限，并开始提及这些文件。

sentences.en: Have you got an email saying you got that from somebody spying on the...
sentences.zh: 你有没有收到一封电子邮件，说你是从某个窥探的人那里得到这个的……

sentences.en: Well, is there such an email, sir?
sentences.zh: 嗯，先生，有这样一封电子邮件吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Well, we'd have to ask the chairman what he has in his confidential material.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们得问问主席他的机密材料里有什么。

sentences.en: And then getting in a back and forth with their Republican counterparts about whether that's proper or not.
sentences.zh: 然后与他们的共和党同僚来回争论这是否合适。

sentences.en: That material's available to everybody.
sentences.zh: 这些材料对每个人都是可用的。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 这就是你所说的吗？

sentences.en: If that's what the chairman's saying, we've got a whole new series of questions.
sentences.zh: 如果主席是这个意思，我们有一系列全新的问题。

sentences.en: No, not if it's committee confidential, but you have that.
sentences.zh: 不，如果是委员会机密则不然，但你拥有它。

sentences.en: I want Judge Kavanaugh to have access so that we can ask him these questions under oath...
sentences.zh: 我希望卡瓦诺法官能够获得权限，以便我们可以在宣誓下向他提出这些问题……

sentences.en: And then overnight, my colleague, Charlie Savage, obtains a lot of the documents, obtains some of these confidential documents.
sentences.zh: 然后一夜之间，我的同事查理·萨维奇获取了大量文件，获取了其中一些机密文件。

sentences.en: And what are some examples of these emails?
sentences.zh: 这些电子邮件有哪些例子？

sentences.en: Well, the one that really jumps out is a discussion of Roe v.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真正跳入眼帘的是对罗诉

sentences.en: Wade, where in the White House counsel's office, he's looking at a draft op-ed piece that women opposed to abortion want to run.
sentences.zh: 韦德案的讨论，在白宫法律顾问办公室里，他在看一份反对堕胎的女性希望发表的专栏文章草稿。

sentences.en: And that draft piece says, it is widely accepted by legal scholars across the board that Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而那篇草稿文章说，法律学者普遍接受罗诉

sentences.en: Wade and its progeny are the settled law of the land.
sentences.zh: 韦德案及其衍生判例是全国既定法律。

sentences.en: And Kavanaugh doesn't like that.
sentences.zh: 而卡瓦诺不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And he responds, I'm not sure that all legal scholars refer to Roe as the settled law of the land at the Supreme Court level, since the court can always overrule its precedent.
sentences.zh: 他回应道，我不确定所有法律学者都在最高法院层面上将罗诉案称为全国既定法律，因为法院总是可以推翻其判例。

sentences.en: And three current justices on the court would do so.
sentences.zh: 而法院现任的三位大法官会这样做。

sentences.en: Now, two things to say about that.
sentences.zh: 现在，关于这一点有两件事要说。

sentences.en: One, it's very interesting because this question of whether he views Roe as settled law has been central to the hearings,
sentences.zh: 第一，这非常有趣，因为他是否将罗诉案视为既定法律这个问题一直是听证会的核心，

sentences.en: central to the interviews he's done as he visited with senators.
sentences.zh: 是他拜访参议员时所做采访的核心。

sentences.en: He says it's settled law.
sentences.zh: 他说这是既定法律。

sentences.en: Not an especially meaningful phrase, but he's adopted it.
sentences.zh: 不是一个特别有意义的短语，但他采用了它。

sentences.en: And here he seems to be saying something different.
sentences.zh: 在这里他似乎在说一些不同的东西。

sentences.en: But the second thing to say is everything he says is exactly accurate.
sentences.zh: 但要说的第二件事是，他说的每一句话都完全准确。

sentences.en: It is the case that not all legal scholars view Roe as settled law.
sentences.zh: 事实确实并非所有法律学者都认为罗诉案是既定法律。

sentences.en: And it was the case at the time that at least three Supreme Court justices were prepared to overrule Roe.
sentences.zh: 当时的情况也确实是至少有三位最高法院大法官准备推翻罗诉案。

sentences.en: So although this sounds pretty hot and although I have no idea why it should have been kept secret,
sentences.zh: 所以虽然这听起来很劲爆，虽然我不知道为什么它应该被保密，

sentences.en: it's not something that actually is going to move the needle at all on people's votes on his confirmation.
sentences.zh: 这实际上根本不会对人们对他的确认投票产生任何影响。

sentences.en: A live picture from Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 来自国会山的实况画面。

sentences.en: Well, this is inside the Hart Senate office building where day three of the Brett Kavanaugh Supreme Court confirmation hearing is about to get underway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里是哈特参议院办公大楼内部，布雷特·卡瓦诺最高法院确认听证会的第三天即将开始。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Judge Kavanaugh answered questions for about 12 hours.
sentences.zh: 周二，卡瓦诺法官回答了大约12个小时的问题。

sentences.en: Chairman Grassley has stated that lawmakers will get 20 minutes each to question the nominee today.
sentences.zh: 格拉斯利主席已经表示，议员今天将各有20分钟时间质询提名人。

sentences.en: So, Adam, day three, Thursday, begins with Democrats having already started to allude to these documents, but very indirectly.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚当，第三天，也就是周四，开始时民主党人已经开始暗示这些文件，但非常间接地。

sentences.en: And the Times having published a story about leaked versions of some of these documents.
sentences.zh: 而且《纽约时报》发表了一篇关于其中一些文件的泄露版本的报道。

sentences.en: So how does that play out once the hearing is underway?
sentences.zh: 那么一旦听证会开始，这会如何发展呢？

sentences.en: The hearing starts out very hot.
sentences.zh: 听证会一开始就非常激烈。

sentences.en: We're rushing through this before me and my colleagues can even read and digest the information.
sentences.zh: 我们在我和我的同事甚至还没来得及阅读和消化信息之前就匆忙推进。

sentences.en: There's high drama.
sentences.zh: 这里有高度的戏剧性。

sentences.en: Can I ask you, can I ask you, can I ask you how long you're going to say the same thing three or four times?
sentences.zh: 我能问你吗，我能问你吗，我能问你打算把同一句话说三四次说多久？

sentences.en: No, sir, I'm saying, I'm saying, I'm saying, I'm saying, I'm knowingly violating the rules.
sentences.zh: 不，先生，我说的是，我说的是，我说的是，我明知故犯地违反了规则。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Senator Kornis called me out for it.
sentences.zh: 科尼斯参议员为此指责了我。

sentences.en: Cory Booker in particular makes a statement.
sentences.zh: 特别是科里·布克发表了一份声明。

sentences.en: I'm saying right now that I'm releasing, I'm releasing committee confidential documents.
sentences.zh: 我现在就说我正在公开，我正在公开委员会机密文件。

sentences.en: Saying he's going to release the documents he thinks the American people have to see.
sentences.zh: 他说他要公开他认为美国人民必须看到的文件。

sentences.en: And I understand that that, the penalty comes with potential ousting from the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我明白，这，惩罚伴随着被驱逐出参议院的潜在可能。

sentences.en: He understands that they're committee confidential and that this may run afoul of some Senate rule.
sentences.zh: 他明白这些是委员会机密，这可能会违反某些参议院规则。

sentences.en: If a senator to suffer expulsion from the body.
sentences.zh: 如果一个参议员遭受被驱逐出该机构的处罚。

sentences.en: And that doing so may actually subject him to expulsion from the Senate.
sentences.zh: 并且这样做实际上可能使他面临被驱逐出参议院的风险。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And apply the rule and bring the charge.
sentences.zh: 并执行规则提出指控。

sentences.en: And that if someone wants to bring charges, so be it, because this is important enough.
sentences.zh: 如果有人想提出指控，那就这样吧，因为这足够重要。

sentences.en: Count me in too.
sentences.zh: 算我一个。

sentences.en: And it's not just Booker.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是布克。

sentences.en: I am releasing that document to the press.
sentences.zh: 我正在将该文件向媒体公开。

sentences.en: Senator Mazie Hirono of Hawaii chimes in and says she's going to disclose documents as well.
sentences.zh: 来自夏威夷的参议员广野庆子插话称她也将披露文件。

sentences.en: I completely agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法。

sentences.en: I concur with what you are doing.
sentences.zh: 我赞同你正在做的事情。

sentences.en: And let's jump into this pit together.
sentences.zh: 让我们一起跳进这个深坑吧。

sentences.en: And it goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 这种情形没完没了。

sentences.en: If you're frustrated with the process, then let's review the Presidential Records Act.
sentences.zh: 如果你对这个过程感到沮丧，那么让我们审查《总统档案法》。

sentences.en: But we're just doing what the law allows us here to do.
sentences.zh: 但我们只是在做法律允许我们在这里做的事情。

sentences.en: And there's back and forth with Republican senators who say this is a gross violation of the way things ought to happen.
sentences.zh: 共和党参议员对此进行了反驳，他们说这是对事情本应发生方式的严重违反。

sentences.en: These documents are not ours.
sentences.zh: 这些文件不是我们的。

sentences.en: They belong to someone else.
sentences.zh: 它们属于别人。

sentences.en: That it's important that secret stuff be kept secret.
sentences.zh: 把机密事情保密是很重要的。

sentences.en: To Senator Booker's point, the document you're talking about has now been approved through the committee processes.
sentences.zh: 正如布克参议员所说，你谈论的那份文件现在已经通过委员会程序批准了。

sentences.en: It's been made public.
sentences.zh: 它已经公开发布了。

sentences.en: The process worked.
sentences.zh: 这个程序起作用了。

sentences.en: And then gradually it emerges that most, if not all, of the documents overnight had been cleared by the committee and President Bush's lawyer to be released.
sentences.zh: 然后渐渐地人们发现，大部分甚至是全部的文件，在一夜之间都得到了委员会和布什总统律师的批准予以公开。

sentences.en: Are you saying, Adam, that Cory Booker had already received permission to publicize these documents by the time he very dramatically went out and said,
sentences.zh: 亚当，你是说科里·布克在他非常戏剧性地走出去说这番话之前，就已经获得批准可以公开这些文件了吗？

sentences.en: I'm risking my career here to disseminate these?
sentences.zh: 我冒着断送职业生涯的风险来传播这些？

sentences.en: No, I don't want to say that.
sentences.zh: 不，我不想这么说。

sentences.en: I think the situation was deeply confusing.
sentences.zh: 我认为情况非常混乱。

sentences.en: I'm not accusing Senator Booker or anyone else of acting in bad faith or dishonestly.
sentences.zh: 我并不是指责布克参议员或其他任何人有恶意或不诚实。

sentences.en: I mean, staffers were working overnight and who knows who was communicating what with whom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，工作人员通宵工作，谁知道谁在和谁沟通什么。

sentences.en: But as the day progressed, it seemed like most, if not all, of the documents did become public.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，看起来大部分甚至是全部文件确实都公开了。

sentences.en: So some of this high drama seems to dissipate.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一些高度戏剧化的场面似乎消散了。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, it conveys this real moment of bitterness and fury on the part of Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，它传达了民主党人内心真正的痛苦和愤怒时刻。

sentences.en: And then as you start to see the documents, you do have to scratch your head and wonder why in the world they were kept secret to begin with.
sentences.zh: 然后当你开始看到这些文件时，你确实不得不挠头，纳闷它们最初到底为什么要保密。

sentences.en: And I asked yesterday if your views on Roe have changed since you were in the White House.
sentences.zh: 我昨天问过，你在白宫之后对罗诉韦德案的看法是否发生了变化。

sentences.en: You said something to the effect that you didn't know what I meant.
sentences.zh: 你说了类似于你不知道我什么意思的话。

sentences.en: And we have an email that was previously marked confidential but is now public and chose that you asked about making edits.
sentences.zh: 我们有一封以前被标记为机密但现在已公开的电子邮件，它显示你曾询问过关于修改的事宜。

sentences.en: But Adam, I wonder, is the reason Democrats are so fixated on these documents, especially a document like that?
sentences.zh: 但亚当，我想知道，为什么民主党人如此执着于这些文件，特别是像这样的一份文件？

sentences.en: I quote, first of all, that Kavanaugh has basically deferred on every question relating to hot button issues like abortion by citing that as a judge,
sentences.zh: 我引用一下，首先，卡瓦诺基本上对有关堕胎等热点问题的每一个问题都进行了推脱，理由是作为一名法官，

sentences.en: it's inappropriate to speculate.
sentences.zh: 进行猜测是不合适的。

sentences.en: I can't say.
sentences.zh: 我不能说。

sentences.en: No other previous judge has talked about it.
sentences.zh: 以前没有别的法官谈论过这个。

sentences.en: So they're looking for any opening, any evidence from his private life or his professional life that he actually has a view on this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在寻找任何突破口，寻找他私生活或职业生活中证明他实际上对这些事情有看法的任何证据。

sentences.en: Yeah, very good point.
sentences.zh: 是的，说得好。

sentences.en: They're trying to leverage some information out of the guy.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图从这家伙身上撬出一些信息。

sentences.en: If you're just going to say, where do you stand on executive power?
sentences.zh: 如果你只是问，你对行政权力持什么立场？

sentences.en: Where do you stand on the Second Amendment?
sentences.zh: 你对第二修正案持什么立场？

sentences.en: Where do you stand on abortion rights?
sentences.zh: 你对堕胎权持什么立场？

sentences.en: The nominee will give canned answers and tell you nothing.
sentences.zh: 被提名人会给出套话，什么也不会告诉你。

sentences.en: So the documents are a way into it.
sentences.zh: 所以这些文件是一个切入点。

sentences.en: So please, once again, tell us why you believe Roe is settled law.
sentences.zh: 所以请再次告诉我们，为什么你认为罗诉韦德案是已成定局的法律。

sentences.en: And if you could, do you believe it is correctly settled?
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，你认为它被恰当地定论了吗？

sentences.en: So thank you, Senator Feinstein.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，范斯坦参议员。

sentences.en: In that draft letter, it was referring to the views of legal scholars.
sentences.zh: 在那份草拟的信中，指的是法学学者的观点。

sentences.en: The Democrats don't have a lot of cards to play.
sentences.zh: 民主党人手里没有多少牌可打。

sentences.en: The documents is the best one in their hand, and they're playing it.
sentences.zh: 文件是他们手中最好的一张牌，他们正在打这张牌。

sentences.en: But it's a long shot.
sentences.zh: 但这希望渺茫。

sentences.en: The votes seem pretty baked in, and Judge Kavanaugh's chances of confirmation continue to be very good.
sentences.zh: 选票似乎已经板上钉钉，卡瓦诺法官获得确认的机会仍然非常好。

sentences.en: So what sort of larger point are Democratic senators trying to make here about these documents?
sentences.zh: 那么民主党参议员试图通过这些文件表达什么更宏大的观点呢？

sentences.en: The documents, Michael, really are a symbol.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这些文件确实是一个象征。

sentences.en: They're a way for Democrats to say, this process is messed up.
sentences.zh: 它们是民主党人表达“这个程序搞砸了”的一种方式。

sentences.en: It's illegitimate.
sentences.zh: 这是非法的。

sentences.en: It's a rush job.
sentences.zh: 这是一次仓促行事。

sentences.en: Important information is being withheld from the American public.
sentences.zh: 重要信息被向美国公众隐瞒。

sentences.en: It's of a piece with the protests that keep breaking out.
sentences.zh: 这与不断爆发的抗议活动是一脉相承的。

sentences.en: President Roosevelt's decision.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福总统的决定。

sentences.en: Justice Jackson.
sentences.zh: 杰克逊大法官。

sentences.en: Every hour of every day of the hearings.
sentences.zh: 听证会每一天的每一个小时。

sentences.en: This is coming out of my time, but that's okay.
sentences.zh: 这占用了我的时间，但没关系。

sentences.en: Let these people have their free speech.
sentences.zh: 让这些人拥有言论自由吧。

sentences.en: Whether Democrats succeed in blocking this nomination or not, and the answer is probably not,
sentences.zh: 无论民主党人能否成功阻止这一提名，答案大概是不能，

sentences.en: they will try to demonstrate to the Democratic base that at this odd moment in history, partisan politics have devolved to a point, they would say,
sentences.zh: 他们将试图向民主党基本盘证明，在历史的这个奇怪时刻，党派政治已经退化到了他们所说的地步，

sentences.en: where a Supreme Court nominee is going to be voted on without careful consideration of his entire record.
sentences.zh: 即在没有仔细审视其全部记录的情况下，就要对最高法院提名人进行投票表决。

sentences.en: And I wonder if the message to the Democratic base is not just that this process has gotten so partisan,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，向民主党基本盘传递的信息不仅是这个过程变得如此党派化，

sentences.en: but that if Democrats are essentially powerless in this moment to stop Kavanaugh from getting on the court,
sentences.zh: 而且如果民主党人在此时此刻基本上无力阻止卡瓦诺进入最高法院，

sentences.en: they are at least willing to stage dramatic protests in a pretty solemn environment of the Senate Judiciary Committee to make a point about this.
sentences.zh: 他们至少愿意在参议院司法委员会这个相当庄严的环境中举行戏剧性的抗议，来就此表明立场。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it may not pay dividends on this particular nomination, but it may energize people in the midterms and beyond.
sentences.zh: 这可能不会对这次特定的提名带来回报，但它可能会在期中选举及以后激发人们的活力。

sentences.en: Judge, when I started this, I said, this is not just about filling a key vacancy on the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 法官阁下，当我开始的时候我说过，这不仅仅是填补最高法院的一个关键空缺。

sentences.en: It's more than the question of release of documents.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是公开文件的问题。

sentences.en: It is really goes to the heart of where we are in America at this moment.
sentences.zh: 它确实触及了我们此刻身处美国的内核。

sentences.en: You have been nominated to be a justice on the United States Supreme Court by President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 你被唐纳德·特朗普总统提名担任美国最高法院大法官。

sentences.en: We have to take your nomination in the context of this moment in history.
sentences.zh: 我们必须在历史的这个时刻的背景下来看待你的提名。

sentences.en: Judge Kavanaugh kept saying, well, I don't want to talk about current events, but current events were in the room.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺法官一直说，嗯，我不想谈论时事，但时事就在房间里。

sentences.en: We're in a moment where the president has shown contempt for the federal judiciary, unlike any president we can recall.
sentences.zh: 我们正处于这样一个时刻：总统对联邦司法机构表现出蔑视，这是我们能想到的任何总统都无法比拟的。

sentences.en: He is a president who is the subject of an active criminal investigation, an investigation which he has apparently sought to obstruct repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 他是一位正受到积极刑事调查的总统，而这项调查他显然曾多次试图阻挠。

sentences.en: He is a president who has been characterized in this hearing publicly on the record as an unindicted co-conspirator.
sentences.zh: 他是一位在这次听证会上被公开指控为未被起诉的共同阴谋者的总统。

sentences.en: And in the last two days or in the course of this hearing, there have been two incredible events, the release of a book and an article in the New York Times,
sentences.zh: 在过去的两天里，或者在这次听证会期间，发生了两件不可思议的事：一本书的出版和《纽约时报》的一篇文章，

sentences.en: which remind us, again, what a serious moment we face in the history of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这再次提醒我们，我们在美国历史上正面临着多么严重的时刻。

sentences.en: And that's why your nomination is different than any.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你的提名与任何提名都不同。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 亚当，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日通讯DealBook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些最有影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Mr. Secretary, I'm sure you've heard the story that's gripping Washington right now.
sentences.zh: 部长先生，我确信你已经听说了现在正吸引华盛顿目光的故事。

sentences.en: It's this anonymous op-ed in the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 就是《纽约时报》这篇匿名专栏文章。

sentences.en: Were you the author of that op-ed?
sentences.zh: 你是那篇专栏文章的作者吗？

sentences.en: Could you comment on it?
sentences.zh: 你能对此发表评论吗？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So it shouldn't surprise anyone that the New York Times, a liberal newspaper that has attacked this administration relentlessly,
sentences.zh: 因此，《纽约时报》这家无情攻击本届政府的自由派报纸选择发表这样一篇文章，不应该让任何人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: chose to print such a piece.
sentences.zh: 选择发表这样一篇文章。

sentences.en: On Thursday, at least a dozen senior officials in the Trump administration, including Vice President Mike Pence, Housing Secretary Ben Carson, and Secretary of State Mike Pompeo,
sentences.zh: 周四，特朗普政府的至少十几位高级官员，包括副总统迈克·彭斯、住房部长本·卡森和国务卿迈克·蓬佩奥，

sentences.en: denied that they had written the anonymous op-ed in the Times, describing efforts to undermine the president from inside the administration.
sentences.zh: 否认他们撰写了《纽约时报》上那篇描述破坏政府内部总统努力的匿名专栏文章。

sentences.en: It is sad that you have someone who would make that choice.
sentences.zh: 令人遗憾的是，竟然会有人做出这种选择。

sentences.en: I come from a place where if you're not in a position to execute the commander's intent, you have a singular option.
sentences.zh: 我来自这样一个地方：如果你没有能力执行长官的意图，你只有一个选择。

sentences.en: It is to leave.
sentences.zh: 那就是离开。

sentences.en: Almost all the officials denounced the publication of the article, saying it was a betrayal of the president.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有官员都谴责该文章的发表，称这是对总统的背叛。

sentences.en: And I'll answer your other question directly, because I know someone will say, gosh, you didn't answer the question.
sentences.zh: 我会直接回答你的另一个问题，因为我知道有人会说，天哪，你没有回答这个问题。

sentences.en: It's not mine.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that six states are now opening investigations into the conduct of the Catholic Church
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》报道称，在宾夕法尼亚州长达数十年的虐童丑闻掩盖报告曝光后，六个州现在开始对天主教会的行为展开调查。

sentences.en: in the wake of an explosive report about its decades-long cover-up of child sex abuse in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州长达数十年的隐瞒儿童性虐待的爆炸性报告之后。

sentences.en: Attorneys general in Illinois, Missouri, Nebraska, New Jersey, New Mexico, and New York say they are demanding records from dioceses in their states
sentences.zh: 伊利诺伊州、密苏里州、内布拉斯加州、新泽西州、新墨西哥州和纽约州的司法部长表示，他们正在要求其所在州的教区提供记录

sentences.en: in response to growing demands from Catholics for greater accountability from church leaders.
sentences.zh: 以回应天主教徒对教会领导人承担更多责任的日益增长的要求。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcombe, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills,
sentences.zh: 《The Daily》由西奥·鲍尔库姆、林赛·加里森、雷切尔·奎斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯、

sentences.en: Ike Sreeze-Kanaraja, Claire Tennesketter, Paige Cowan, Michael Simon-Johnson, and Jessica Chung, with editing help from Larissa Anderson.
sentences.zh: 艾克·斯里兹-卡纳拉贾、克莱尔·特内斯凯特、佩奇·科万、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊和杰西卡·钟制作，拉里萨·安德森提供编辑帮助。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制作人。

sentences.en: Samantha Hennig is our editorial director.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的编辑总监。

sentences.en: Our technical manager is Brad Fisher.
sentences.zh: 我们的技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔。

sentences.en: Our engineer is Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 我们的工程师是克里斯·伍德。

sentences.en: And our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sam Dolnick, Michaela Bouchard, and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔尼克、米凯拉·布沙尔和斯特拉·陈。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《The Wirecutter Show》节目中，我们正在为节日期间的款待做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目获取让您的客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到不省人事才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有对什么过敏或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序上或在您喜欢的任何地方收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
